overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 15
overview.text: In this lesson, you will investigate compound sentences. A compound sentence joined by 'and' is true only when both constituent sentences are true (intersection), while a compound sentence joined by 'or' is true when at least one constituent sentence is true (union).
outcomes: Describe the solution set of two equations or inequalities joined by the connective 'and' as the intersection of their individual solution sets.
Describe the solution set of two equations or inequalities joined by the connective 'or' as the union of their individual solution sets.
Graph compound sentences on the real number line.
overview.teacherInsight: Connect 'and' to simultaneous conditions (both must hold) and 'or' to alternative choices (at least one must hold). In logic, mathematical 'or' is always inclusive unless stated otherwise.

content.html:
Compound Sentence Intersection & Union Visualizer

Toggle between AND (Intersection $\cap$) and OR (Union $\cup$) for the sentence: $x - 15 = 5$ [connective] $2x + 5 = 1$.

Sentence 1: $x - 15 = 5$ x = 20
Sentence 2: $2x + 5 = 1$ x = -2
Compound Solution Set:
{-2, 20}
Under OR: Any value that makes EITHER equation true is a solution.

vocabulary.definition: A compound sentence that is true only if both of its component statements are simultaneously true. Corresponding to set intersection (∩).
A compound sentence that is true if at least one of its component statements is true. Corresponding to set union (∪).
The set of elements belonging to both sets A and B (A ∩ B).
The set of elements belonging to set A, set B, or both (A ∪ B).

practiceQuestions.question: Solve the compound sentence $x - 15 = 5 \text{ or } 2x + 5 = 1$ and identify the complete solution set:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
$x - 15 = 5 \implies x = 20$
$2x + 5 = 1 \implies 2x = -4 \implies x = -2$
Because the statements are joined by 'or', the solution set contains the union of both solutions: $\{-2, 20\}$.

practiceQuestions.question: How does the solution set of $x < 1 \text{ and } x > -1$ compare to the solution set of $x < 1 \text{ or } x > -1$?
options: The 'and' condition restricts solutions to $-1 < x < 1$, while the 'or' condition includes all real numbers $(-\infty, \infty)$.
Both compound sentences have the exact same solution set.
The 'and' condition includes all real numbers, while the 'or' condition has no solution.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An 'and' compound statement represents the intersection (numbers between -1 and 1). An 'or' compound statement represents the union; every real number is either greater than -1 or less than 1, covering the entire real number line.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 15 Exit Ticket: Solution Sets of Two or More Equations Joined by 'And' or 'Or'
exitTicket.prompt: Solve the system, and graph the solution set on a number line: x - 15 = 5 or 2x + 5 = 1. Write a compound inequality for acceptable swimming pool chlorine levels between 1 ppm and 3 ppm inclusive. Explain how changing 'and' to 'or' in x < 1 and x > -1 alters the solution set.
exitTicket.solution:
1) x - 15 = 5 => x = 20. 2x + 5 = 1 => 2x = -4 => x = -2. Solution set: {-2, 20}.
2) Chlorine compound inequality: 1 <= x <= 3.
3) 'x < 1 and x > -1' requires both statements to be true, yielding the interval (-1, 1). Changing to 'x < 1 or x > -1' requires either statement to be true; since every real number is either < 1 or > -1, the solution set is all real numbers.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Compound Inequalities with 'And' (Intersection) vs. 'Or' (Union)
guidedExercises.problem:
Graph and state the solution set for:
1) $x > -3$ and $x \le 4$
2) $x < -2$ or $x \ge 3$
3) $x < 1$ and $x > 5$
guidedExercises.scaffolding: 'And' means intersection $\cap$ (elements satisfying BOTH inequalities simultaneously). 'Or' means union $\cup$ (elements satisfying AT LEAST ONE inequality).

steps.label: Analyze Conjunction: $x > -3$ and $x \le 4$
steps.explanation: The overlap between the two rays forms a single bounded segment.

steps.label: Analyze Disjunction: $x < -2$ or $x \ge 3$
steps.explanation: Two separate rays pointing in opposite directions.

steps.label: Analyze Impossible Conjunction: $x < 1$ and $x > 5$
steps.explanation: No number on the real line is simultaneously less than 1 and greater than 5.

guidedExercises.commonPitfall: Writing $5 < x < 1$ or combining disjunctions into a single chain. Chains like $a < x < b$ strictly represent 'and' conjunctions where $a < b$.

problems.prompt:
Consider the compound inequality 0 < x < 3.
(a) Rewrite the inequality as a compound sentence using 'and' or 'or'.
(b) Graph the solution set on a number line.
(c) What happens if the connective word is changed to 'or'?
problems.solution:
(a) x > 0 and x < 3.
(b) An open interval between 0 and 3 with open circles at 0 and 3 and shading in between.
(c) The sentence 'x > 0 or x < 3' is satisfied by every real number because every number is either greater than 0 or less than 3 (or both). The solution set becomes all real numbers.

problems.prompt: Solve the compound sentence: 2x - 4 > 6 or 3x + 1 < -8. Express the solution set in interval and set notation.
problems.solution:
First inequality: 2x > 10 \implies x > 5.
Second inequality: 3x < -9 \implies x < -3.
Union: x < -3 or x > 5.
Set notation: {x \text{ real} \mid x < -3 \text{ or } x > 5}. Interval notation: (-\infty, -3) \cup (5, \infty).
